data.gender_notes: Fihaad is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Fihaad is derived from the Arabic word 'Fihad', which refers to a struggle or striving, particularly in the context of defending one's faith or community. It connotes a sense of bravery and commitment to a just cause. The name Fihaad carries the meaning “One who fights for truth” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Fihaad usually hope their child will grow to embody one who fights for truth and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: In Islamic tradition, 'Fihaad' relates to the concept of striving in the way of God, as mentioned in the Quran (e.g., Surah An-Nisa, Verse 95).
data.etymology: Fihaad belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “One who fights for truth.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Fihaad total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_urdu.name: فیحاد
